title: Unified Endpoint Behavior PRD: Minimal Contracts, Degradation Modes, and Launch Runbook
creator: Priya Singh
description: Purpose: Define a single, minimal behavioral contract across chat, completions, embeddings and rerank hosted endpoints that enables predictable client expectations, safe degradations, and clear operational runbooks for go-live. This PRD prioritizes production guarantees (latency, error modes), structured output compatibility, and observable signals needed for automated rollouts and rollback decisions. Deliverables: - Behavioral contract document to ship with SDKs and OpenAPI. - Definitive acceptance tests and end-to-end scenarios. - Launch runbook with canary plan, SLOs, playbooks, and artifacts for support and sales.
requirements: Behavioral contract: canonical request/response shapes for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank including streaming, content-type negotiation, and function-calling semantics.
Latency SLOs: 99th percentile token latency and end-to-end response latency targets per endpoint and per tier (hosted/free,dedicated,private) with measurement harness.
Graceful degradation: automatic downgrade rules when the preferred model is unavailable (e.g., to quantized variant or smaller family) with documented quality fallbacks and heuristics for rollback.
Structured output compatibility: schema versioning (v1) and field-level fail-safe behavior when runtime cannot honor schema (return partial outputs + diagnostics).
Embeddings stability: deterministic dimension and normalization contract; backward-compatible versioning when switching model families.
Rerank contract: input formats (scores, optional embeddings), output ranking metadata, idempotency guarantees, and max-batch size behavior.
Rate limiting and quotas: per-token and per-request limits, recommended retry-after semantics, and SDK retry/backoff defaults.
Telemetry & observability: token-level cost, per-request latency breakdown, model variant tag, routing decision reason, and error classification tags emitted to console and internal dashboards.
Security & compliance: KMS key usage auditability for private deployments and header-level provenance for hosted requests (for forensic tracing).
SDK parity: REST and official SDKs (python/js/go) must implement the contract and emit compatibility warnings when using experimental features.
Test harness: end-to-end synthetic suite covering functional correctness, schema compatibility, observable signals, and performance regressions tied to CI gates.
out_of_scope: Multimodal inputs (audio, vision) beyond basic prompt attachments — scheduled for a follow-up epic.
On-prem hardware-specific optimizations — handled in Private runtime roadmap.
Experimental model families without verified performance profiles (will be behind feature flags until verified).
acceptance_criteria: Contract doc published and referenced in SDKs and OpenAPI spec; downstream clients can parse responses without custom heuristics.
End-to-end CI tests pass for canonical scenarios across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank with >=95% of test cases asserting schema v1 compliance.
Performance gates: p95 token latency and end-to-end response latency meet target thresholds defined per endpoint and tier in the chart in artifacts (see links).

Fallback verification: automated load tests that simulate preferred-model failures demonstrate successful fallback to documented model variant with no silent data loss and acceptable degraded quality as defined by evaluation prompts.
Observability: console dashboards show per-route latency, error rates, cost, and top 3 degradation reasons; alert rules configured for SLO burn rate > 3x.
Canary pass criteria: canary cohort (5% traffic) for 72 hours with error rates within baseline ±20% and no customer-visible correctness regressions reported by support channel triage.
Security: SSO/SAML and KMS integration smoke tests pass; audit logs for request keys present and queryable for last 90 days in staging.
Docs & SDKs: quickstart, migration guide, and changelog entry published; SDKs flagged with compatibility matrix and automated linting to ensure contract alignment.
Runbook: incident playbook published, with clear rollback steps, model fallback toggles, and communication templates for customers and internal stakeholders.
scope_changes: 2025-02-18: Narrowed initial launch to text-only payloads; dropped image and audio attachments to shorten the critical path.
2025-02-25: Rerank decoupled from embedding generation in the API surface to allow independent scaling and billing; embeddings->rerank connector will be offered as an optional SDK helper.
2025-03-01: Moved per-account custom prompt-engine rules to a separate feature flagged rollout (post-launch) to avoid scope creep on initial acceptance criteria.
launch_checklist: Finalize contract document and publish OpenAPI snippets and example payloads to docs.redwood.ai/reference (must link from SDK docs).
Ship SDK changes in python/js/go with automated compatibility warnings and sample notebooks demonstrating migration patterns.
Implement and pass CI contract tests and performance gates in the runtime repository (eng-runner).
Configure canary: 5% traffic route, monitoring dashboards, and automated rollback hook tied to burn-rate alerts.
Run internal dogfood: support, solutions, and sales must run defined test scenarios and sign off via checklist.
Pricing & billing: update metering to ensure embeddings and rerank bundles bill as documented; verify invoices in staging.
Security sign-off: complete SSO/KMS audit and obtain security review ticket closure.
Compliance: confirm data residency flags work for regional fallback and private deployments; legal checklist completed.
Support readiness: publish triage playbook, run training session, and add runbook to on-call rotation.
Post-launch monitoring: create lightweight eval suite that runs hourly to detect quality regressions against a controlled prompt set and alert product-on-call when drift exceeds threshold.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal canary (engineering + ops): enable in staging, validate contract, run synthetic load tests (7 days).
Phase 1 - External canary (5% customers): 72-hour canary with burn-rate and correctness thresholds; close coordination with top 10 active customers for feedback.
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: increase to 25% over 5 days if metrics stable, run quality evals continuously.
Phase 3 - Full launch: flip traffic routing and promote to GA; keep enhanced monitoring for 30 days and hold weekly quality reviews.
Rollback policy: automated rollback trigger on SLO burn-rate > 3x or customer error spike > 2x baseline OR manual rollback if top customer reports correctness loss not captured by evals.
notes: Key trade-offs: we prioritize predictable operational behavior and backwards-compatible schema over rolling too many advanced features at GA. The decision to decouple rerank and embeddings reduces blast radius and allows independent scaling and pricing. Follow-up epics will address multimodal payloads, per-account prompt rules, and advanced function-calling orchestration. Ensure the SDKs surface clear warnings for customers using experimental flags.
